answer:
ANSWER: Approximately 2,563 genes are significantly differentially expressed (padj < 0.05, up + down) — up-regulated 2,226, down-regulated 337 — when comparing ASXL1 (disease) vs Control with design ~ condition and apeglm LFC shrinkage. This is a Python DESeq2-equivalent estimate; the authoritative DESeq2/apeglm value is produced by the primary R script (analysis.R). Best-estimate range across dispersion choices: ~1,500–2,600.

IMPORTANT EXECUTION NOTE (per your firm directive): I re-confirmed at execution time that R / DESeq2 / apeglm is GENUINELY ABSENT in this workspace (no Rscript anywhere on disk, no conda/apt, and no network to install it). So I could not run analysis.R here. Following your instruction, I executed the documented Python fallback (de_final.py) and am flagging the approximation risk. analysis.R is written and ready to run unchanged in the R-provisioned runner.

WHAT I DID (executed):
- Parsed the space-delimited featureCounts table (60,662 genes x 21 samples); kept the 19 samples present in coldata (dropped MGD1640B, MGD1641B, which have no condition metadata); 8 ASXL1 vs 11 Control.
- Mapped rows to gene_name via gencode gene_id (1:1).
- Median-of-ratios size factors; negative-binomial Wald test for the condition coefficient (delta-method SE using a DESeq2-style dispersion trend log(disp)=0.920-0.492*log(mean)); Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over all 60,662 genes. apeglm shrinkage changes only the LFC, not padj, so the padj<0.05 count is unaffected by it.
- Zero-handling mirrors DESeq2: all-zero genes (10,898) are not tested (p=1); genes expressed in only one group (7,634) get a tiny pseudo-count for a stable log2FC; the 42,130 genes expressed in both groups are tested with no pseudo-count (≈ the DESeq2 MLE).
- RESULT: 2,563 genes with padj<0.05 (up 2,226 / down 337). Sensitivity: uniform pseudo-count=0.1 -> 2,297; gene-specific MoM dispersion -> 1,520.

WHY THE NUMBER IS LARGE: the ASXL1 group is almost all children (ages 4-29) while Control is almost all adults (42-60). A design of ~ condition (as you specified) does not control for age, so it captures a large age/immune transcriptome shift. Top hits are immune/inflammatory and mitochondrial genes (JCHAIN, IGHG1, CLEC12A, APOBEC3B, GAS6-AS1, S100A9, C4BPA, MT-ND5), which is consistent with that confound.

LIMITATIONS / APPROXIMATION RISK: (1) No R/DESeq2 here, so this is a Python reimplementation of the DESeq2 core, not DESeq2 itself; the exact count can differ from DESeq2 (dispersion estimation, independent-filtering heuristic, and Wald-test details). (2) The count is sensitive to the dispersion model (1,520-2,563). (3) I could not verify against real DESeq2 output. Run analysis.R in the R-provisioned runner for the definitive number.

payload.method: Python DESeq2-equivalent (NB Wald + median-of-ratios size factors + DESeq2-style dispersion trend + BH FDR); apeglm LFC shrinkage does not affect padj
payload.answer: Approximately 2,563 genes (up 2,226, down 337); range ~1,500-2,600; definitive value from DESeq2/apeglm via analysis.R
